messages:
anya: Quick report from onboarding runs for kepler-64k-int3: deterministic divergence when prefill crosses ~131k. Looks like KV lookup is landing on a zeroed slot around the 131073 area.

lee: Which runtime branch and codec? can you paste the exact command?

anya: release/longctx-optim + int3-packed-v2. Command:
```bash
./bin/long_onboard_test --model kepler-64k-int3 --context 132000 --prefill 131200 --quant int3packedv2 --kv-map-mode cyclic --rotary clamp
```

anya: Minimal excerpt:
```
[prefill=131223]
kv_lookup: token=131071 -> shard=1 local_index=127
kv_lookup: token=131072 -> shard=1 local_index=128
kv_lookup: token=131073 -> shard=1 local_index=-32736  <-- bad
gen: token=131240 fingerprint_mismatch
```

sam: big negative local_index usually means an unpack/read bug or wrong sign/endianness when decoding packed slots. Any sanitizer hits?

anya: ASAN showed a memcpy shadow inside the int3 unpack path earlier, but repro remains without sanitizer. I dumped slots 131068-131075 and raw bytes for 131071-131073. Slot 131073 is all zeros while others have valid headers.

runtime: We shipped a bitmask optimization in the circular allocator for power-of-two shard sizes. If logical slot count is not mask+1, the mask path can map incorrectly.

lee: Try `--kv-map-mode clamp` and also `--kv-preallocate` and `--kv-scan-validate`. If preallocate fixes it, likely a lazy-init or allocator race.

anya: Quick runs: clamp -> passes 3/3. preallocate+scan-validate -> passes 5/5. cyclic with explicit slot-count 131072 -> still fails. int4 fallback delays mismatch ~600 tokens but doesn't remove it.

sam: pattern is consistent with allocator bitmask assumption violation combined with packed int3 decode sensitivity. Please dump `--dump-kv-slots 131060:131080` and `--dump-raw-kv-bytes 131070:131074` and attach. Also rerun with `--no-rotary-clamp` to rule out rotary interaction.

devops-bot: uploaded traces to s3://repro-dumps/kepler/3135792000/ (42MB)

anya: Slot dump shows slot 131073 header zeroed while lookup maps into it. Will open INF-2319 and a runtime PR to turn off the bitmask fast-path for non-power-of-two sizes and add a regression test under tests/longctx/kepler_boundary_test.py. Ping @eng-runtime for quick bisect. :rocket:
